newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss split over fate of crayfish invaders.
newsitem.headline: Swiss split over fate of crayfish invaders.

text.p: An invasion of ravenous American crayfish in a small lake has split Switzerland's biggest canton into opposing camps -- authorities who want to poison the crustaceans and local residents who want to eat them.

Both sides agree the smaller freshwater relatives of the lobster must go because they threaten to devour most of the fish, bugs and plants in the pond in a wealthy suburb of Zurich, the city that gives the surrounding canton its name.
Cantonal officials want to spray a strong insecticide named Fenthion to wipe out the species, native to North America and a speciality of Louisiana cooking in the southern United States.

But local residents are worried about the danger of even small quantities of nerve poison and are petitioning the canton to use fishing nets instead, combining the goal of crayfish eradication with a culinary reward.
"We've caught 1,200 so far and sold them to a nearby restaurant as a delicacy," said Alfred Egli from the local Schuebel Pond Protection Committee.

The crayfish native to North America are bigger and more aggressive than local crayfish, which they have mostly eaten since being introduced somehow to the pond in the late 1980s, cantonal authorities say.
